passage:
Thursday.
Today Yash sat with Dev again at lunch, and they laughed at a joke I did not hear. I ate fast and read my book. My cousin said "just ignore it" on the phone. That made me feel worse, like there was nothing to say.
In the evening Mum came and sat on my bed. "You have been quiet, Lokesh. Want to tell me?"
So I did. She said friendships shift and stretch, that this doesn't mean it is over, and that she would always be close by. I cried a little. 😢
I still feel sad, but I do not feel so alone.
Lokesh

qa.q: Who did Yash sit with at lunch?
Why did Lokesh feel worse after his cousin said "just ignore it"?
qa.a: It left Lokesh alone with the hurt, as if there was nothing to say.

qa.q: What did Mum do that helped Lokesh?
qa.a: She noticed he was quiet, sat on his bed, listened, and said friendships shift and stretch and that she would be close by.

qa.q: How might Lokesh's cousin have meant the advice?
qa.a: The cousin probably meant to help Lokesh not to fret, though it did not make Lokesh feel heard.

grounding: A child is quiet after a friend gets a new friend; the child's mum listens and says friendships shift and stretch, so he feels heard.
